fixes.explanation: Yes, ma'am, yes, sir. The text says no such Passover had been observed “…from the days of the judges who had governed Israel through all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah.” Think about how long that stretch is. It starts with the judges and runs through the kings of Israel and Judah, and this Passover in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign is the one the text sets apart.

Solomon is a big name, so I get the pick. But the text goes back even further than that. It says no such Passover had been observed “…from the days of the judges who had governed Israel through all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah.” So the clock starts at the judges.

You got it, baker. The text says Josiah removed the mediums and spiritists, the household gods and idols, and “…all the abominations that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem.” Notice it says all the abominations, not just a few. I think Josiah wasn't skipping anything.

Nothing in this verse is about traders, friend. The text says Josiah removed the mediums and spiritists, the household gods and idols, and all the abominations seen in Judah and Jerusalem. The verse doesn't mention traders or their goods. What it names are the mediums and idols.

No priests or singers are named as cleared out here, friend. The text says Josiah removed the mediums and spiritists, the household gods and idols, and all the abominations seen in Judah and Jerusalem. The verse doesn't mention priests or singers being removed at all.

Right on, baker. Josiah did all of this to carry out “the words of the law written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.” He didn't stop at hearing it. He carried it out. That's what all the clearing out was for.

Good thinking, friend, but the verse says law. Josiah did this to carry out “the words of the law written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.” So the clearing out in this verse comes back to what that book says.

Nice song pick, friend, but the verse says law. Josiah did this to carry out “the words of the law written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.” So the clearing out wasn't about songs. It was about carrying out what that book says.

That's right, baker. Josiah turned to the LORD with all his heart, soul and strength, “…according to all the Law of Moses.” All his heart, all his soul, all his strength, and the whole Law. I can barely finish a whole batch without a snack break.
David is a name that comes to mind, friend. But the verse says Josiah turned to the LORD “…according to all the Law of Moses.” So the name tied to the Law here is Moses.
Solomon is a famous name, friend. But the verse says Josiah turned to the LORD “…according to all the Law of Moses.” That's the Law he was following with all his heart, soul and strength.

That's him, baker. The text says the anger was “…kindled against Judah because of all that Manasseh had done to provoke Him to anger.” Manasseh was a king of Judah before Josiah (2 Kings 21:1). The writer doesn't hide whose doing this was.
That's it, baker. The LORD had said, “I will remove Judah from My sight, just as I removed Israel.” That's heavy, and I think it hurts to read. It's what He had already said.

Right, baker. The text says Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt marched up to help the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River. The king of Assyria is the one Neco is going to help. Josiah then goes out to confront Neco, and that's the next turn in the story.

Babylon is a good guess, friend, but that's not who this verse names. The text says Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt “marched up to help the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River.” And it's Josiah who goes out to confront Neco.

Edom is a fair guess, friend, but that's not who this verse names. The text says Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt “marched up to help the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River.” That's where Neco is headed when King Josiah goes out to confront him.
You got it, baker. The text calls him “…Jehoahaz son of Josiah…” The people of the land took him, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father. So a son takes his father's place.

No priest in this verse, friend. The text says the people of the land took “…Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.” So he's Josiah's son, taking the throne in place of his father.

I get why you'd wonder with Neco in the story, friend. But the text says the people of the land took “…Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.” So he's called Josiah's son. Nothing in this verse ties him to Neco.
